source: Del et al. (2026) How Uncertainty Estimation Scales with Sampling in Reasoning Models
finding: Three reasoning models, 17 tasks. A single verbalized confidence (VC) already discriminates well. Self-consistency (SC) starts below VC at equal sample count and does not overtake it up to K=8. This reverses the 2023 finding for non-reasoning models.
numbers: VC@1 AUROC 78.8 MMLU-Pro Math, 68.7 GSM8K, 73.8 STEM avg, 68.5 humanities avg. SC@2: 70.5 math, 66.6 STEM, 63.3 humanities (VC@2 math 73.5). SC@2 on MMLU-Pro Math 65.9 and GSM8K 63.3. VC scales 71.3 (K=1) to 81.4 (K=8) in math (+10.1), +4.6 STEM, +4.1 humanities, saturating by about K=5 outside math. Matched-token test with gpt-oss-20b: SC weaker under extended reasoning than under shallow generation.
quote: self-consistency exhibits lower initial discrimination and lags behind verbalized confidence under moderate sampling
limits: Only three models; VC is aggregated over samples with the majority answer; AIME VC is low (66.4) and prompt-sensitive; AUROC only, no ECE.
agent_relevance: For a reasoning-model agent, do not assume agreement beats self-report. Ask for a short verbalized confidence at end of chain AND sample 2+; use both.

source: Del et al. (2026) How Uncertainty Estimation Scales with Sampling in Reasoning Models (hybrid and domain results)
finding: Combining VC and SC beats either alone, even when either is given a much larger budget. Gains depend on domain: biggest in math (the RLVR-trained domain).
numbers: Hybrid (SCVC) with two samples improves AUROC by up to +12 on average; +12.9 in math, +6.4 in STEM/humanities at K=2; SCVC math gains continue (+2.7 further) while STEM and humanities saturate earlier. Six elicitation variants tested; domain-averaged AUROC about 70.6 to 77.2 (VeEl 70.80 math, 76.95 STEM, 70.61 humanities; VaEl highest 77.2).
limits: Same three models; mixing weight tuned on their data.
agent_relevance: Cheap default: two samples plus verbalized confidence, combined. More samples past about 5 give little outside math.

source: Mei et al. (2025) Reasoning about Uncertainty: Do Reasoning Models Know When They Do Not Know?
finding: Reasoning models (o3-Mini, DeepSeek R1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Gemini) are overconfident in verbalized confidence, especially on hard graduate-level tasks and on wrong answers. Deeper reasoning effort raises overconfidence on wrong answers. A second introspection pass helps some models and hurts others.
numbers: Confidence on wrong answers often above 85% (5% increments). ECE strongly negatively correlated with accuracy across models; Claude weaker (r=-0.69). o3-Mini ECE up 7 points absolute from low to high reasoning effort vs 2 for Claude. One setting: low to high depth gave +10.8% accuracy and -5.5% ECE (a benchmark where accuracy rises). Models above 90% accuracy on ARC-Challenge and MMLU, 10-20 points lower on StrategyQA and GPQA, under 40% on the newest hard sets. Introspective UQ improves o3-Mini and R1, worsens Claude 3.7 Sonnet.
quote: reasoning models are typically overconfident, with self-verbalized confidence estimates often greater than 85% particularly for incorrect responses
limits: Calibration metric (ECE) not AUROC; prompt engineering helped little for reasoning models; 2025 model vintage.
agent_relevance: More thinking does not mean better self-knowledge. Do not trust end-of-chain confidence after a long chain without an external or sample check.

source: Cacioli (2026) Domain-level metacognitive monitoring in frontier LLMs: a 33-model atlas
finding: Type-2 AUROC of verbalized confidence varies by domain inside each model, so one aggregate number hides weak domains. Calibration does not transfer evenly across task types.
numbers: 33 models, 1,500 MMLU items (250 per domain, six domains), 47,151 observations. Aggregate AUROC from .498 (Gemma 3 1B) to .806 (Opus 4.6). Applied/Professional easiest (mean .742), Formal Reasoning .658 and Natural Science .652 hardest; middle three domains within .007. Anthropic aggregate .708-.806 across four generations but profile shapes differ. GPT-oss-120B confidence SD 21.3 yet AUROC .530. Median bootstrap CI width .199 per cell. Split-half aggregate stability r=.893. Earlier work cited there: Sonnet 4.6 .965 on Executive Function but .485 on Prospective Regulation.
limits: Single author, MMLU only, verbalized confidence only, wide cell CIs; six-domain grouping is pragmatic not a validated construct.
agent_relevance: A per-task-type calibration table is justified, but entries are noisy and model-specific; refit when the model changes and keep it coarse (math, code, factual, open-ended).

source: Yuan et al. (2026) Hidden Error Awareness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
finding: Hidden states predict whether a reasoning trace is wrong far better than the model's stated confidence. In these open models, SC beats VC (opposite to Del).
numbers: Linear probe AUROC 0.95 for trace correctness; 0.79 from the first reasoning step; verbalized confidence 0.67; self-consistency 0.82; CCS 0.72; text-surface classifier 0.59. Wrong traces say 4.55/5, correct 4.87/5. 65% of wrong traces are high stated confidence with high internal error score. DeepSeek-R1 probe 0.852. Nine models 1.5B-72B (Qwen, Llama, Phi). Steering, probe-guided best-of-N, self-correction and activation patching all failed to fix errors.
limits: Needs hidden-state access; mostly small open models with a 1-5 confidence scale, which may explain lower VC than Del's frontier-model numbers.
agent_relevance: A black-box agent cannot use probes. Where VC is weak (small models), use SC; the ordering of VC vs SC depends on model class.

source: Sethi (2026) Do Not Overthink It: Inter-Rollout Action Agreement (TrACE)
finding: Per-step agreement among sampled next actions can allocate compute adaptively in an agent loop without any verifier.
numbers: Qwen 2.5 3B Instruct on CPU. TrACE-4 matches SC-4 accuracy with 33% fewer calls on GSM8K (n=50) and 39% fewer on MiniHouse (n=30 tasks x 3 seeds). TrACE-8 matches SC-8 with 55% fewer (GSM8K) and 65% fewer (MiniHouse) calls. Steps with agreement at or above 0.8 are over-represented in successful tasks; steps below 0.4 mostly in failing tasks.
limits: Tiny samples, 3B model, toy household environment, agreement-success shown as a figure with no AUROC; not frontier-model evidence.
agent_relevance: Per-step agreement is a plausible gate for when to spend more samples in an agent loop, but unproven for frontier agents.

source: Aghazadeh et al. (2026) CGES: Confidence-Guided Early Stopping for Self-Consistency
finding: Bayesian early stopping over answer posteriors cuts samples while matching majority vote. It needs a scalar confidence per sample: token probabilities or a reward model, not a verbalized number.
numbers: Across five reasoning benchmarks, average calls fall 58% (16.0 to 6.7) with accuracy within 0.4 points of self-consistency. MATH500 2.88 calls, GSM8K 1.25 calls for the matched variants (+0.4 and +0.7 pp). Token-probability confidences cluster near 0.9 and need rescaling.
limits: Tested variants rely on logprobs or a process reward model. A pure black-box API without logprobs is not covered; no verbalized-confidence variant found in the text. Count-only Adaptive-Consistency (earlier evidence) is the logprob-free option.
agent_relevance: Without logprobs use answer-count stopping (Adaptive-Consistency) or a verbalized scalar; loss for the latter is untested here.

source: Stav et al. (2026) When Does Intrinsic Self-Correction Help? A Task-Sensitive Analysis
finding: Without external feedback, a revise pass helps a lot when the task has checkable constraints, and can hurt on open reasoning. Contradicts the blanket 2023 negative result for newer models.
numbers: Five LLMs (Mistral Large 2512, Claude Haiku 4.5, DeepSeek V3.1, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, Gemini 3 Pro). SAT: Haiku 75.64 to 93.59, Mistral 34.62 to 64.96, Gemini Pro 97.00 to 100; average 65.66% of baseline errors removed. BBEH non-choice: Mistral 17.04 to 25.67, Gemini Pro 80.88 to 82.30. HLE text choice: Mistral 9.50 to 26.50, Haiku 11.00 to 34.50. Correct-to-wrong flips at most 2.1% on SAT but up to 13.25% on BBEH and HLE. Smaller gains for the strongest model.
limits: The SAT revise prompt lets the model verify explicit constraints, close to external checking; LLM judges for open tasks; baselines not matched on token cost.
agent_relevance: Revise when the claim can be checked against explicit constraints; guard against wrong flips (keep original unless the check fails) on open reasoning.

source: Kaddour et al. (2026) Agentic Uncertainty Reveals Agentic Overconfidence
finding: Coding agents on real repair tasks predict their own success far too high and discriminate barely above chance, before, during or after the work.
numbers: 100 SWE-Bench Pro tasks, mini-swe-agent. True success: GPT-5.2-Codex 35%, Gemini-3-Pro 22%, Claude Opus 4.5 27%. Estimated success up to 77% for an agent that succeeds 22%. Pre-execution AUROC: GPT 0.62 [0.50,0.75], Claude 0.64 [0.49,0.78], Gemini about 0.53; post-execution GPT 0.58, Claude 0.55, Gemini 0.51. Mid-execution AUROC GPT 0.53 stable, Gemini 0.49 to 0.64, Claude 0.62 to 0.52. Agents 5.5x more likely to confidently predict success on a failing task than to doubt a passing one.
limits: Wide bootstrap CIs; pairwise differences not significant; one benchmark (code repair).
agent_relevance: Self-estimated task success is not usable as a gate. A hard external signal (tests) must carry the decision.

source: Kaddour et al. (2026) adversarial review result (same paper)
finding: Showing the finished patch anchors the reviewer on plausibility. Framing the review as bug-finding lowers overconfidence. Not seeing the patch (pre-execution) discriminated at least as well as seeing it.
numbers: Overconfident-failure rate falls from 72% (standard review) to 45% (adversarial). Adversarial AUROC: Claude 0.55 to 0.64, Gemini 0.51 to 0.57, GPT unchanged (0.55). Best ECE with adversarial prompting. For GPT the shift is a uniform offset fixable by Platt scaling (ECE 0.01 vs 0.30).
limits: Hiding the earlier answer was not tested directly; pre-execution removes the whole solution, not just the earlier answer. Differences not significant.
agent_relevance: In review, ask the model to find bugs first, or review without sight of its own solution. Direct evidence for hiding the earlier answer is still thin.

source: Ravuri and Amarasinghe (2025) Eliminating Hallucination-Induced Errors in LLM Code Generation with Functional Clustering
finding: Execute sampled programs on self-generated inputs, cluster by behavior; the largest cluster mass is a confidence score that gates answering. A hard check (execution) turns agreement into a usable selective-answer rule.
numbers: GPT-4o and Claude-3-Haiku, 50 programs per task, HumanEval and LiveCodeBench. LiveCodeBench: returned-answer error rate 65% to 2%; at a strict threshold 0% error while answering 15.6% of prompts; 2% error answers 36.8%.
limits: Older, non-reasoning models; coverage cost is large; remaining errors are spec misreadings, so agreement cannot catch shared misunderstanding. No head-to-head against self-report AUROC extracted.
agent_relevance: Confidence can gate when to run a check, but the check (execution) does the work. Count tokens: 50 samples is costly.

source: Harshavardhan (2026) Self-Anchoring Calibration Drift in LLMs
finding: Building on one's own prior outputs across turns shifts expressed confidence, but in model-specific directions; the pre-registered uniform hypothesis was not supported.
numbers: 150 questions, three models (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.2), three conditions. Sonnet 4.6: mean confidence drift -0.032, t(14)=-2.43, p=.029, d=-0.627; ECE drift F(4,56)=22.77, p<.001, eta2=.791. GPT-5.2: +0.026 in open-ended domains, ECE rising by turn 5. Gemini 3.1 Pro: no significant drift (t(14)=0.38, p=.710).
limits: Single author, 15 items per cell in the tests; no hide-the-answer condition.
agent_relevance: Multi-turn loops change confidence unpredictably; recompute confidence from fresh samples each round instead of carrying it.

source: Yona, Aharoni and Geva (2024) Can LLMs Faithfully Express Their Intrinsic Uncertainty in Words?
finding: Wording of answers (hedges, decisiveness) does not track the model's internal sample-consistency confidence. Prompting for hedges helps little.
numbers: Faithfulness metric cMFG (0.5 is the random baseline): vanilla prompts 0.52-0.57 across five models (GemNano, GemPro, GemUltra, GPT-3.5, GPT-4); best prompted cells 0.70 and 0.63; most 0.51-0.59. Intrinsic confidence estimated by sampling agreement.
limits: LLM-judge based metric; 2024 models; knowledge QA; no before/after RLHF comparison in the text read.
agent_relevance: Do not read tone or hedges as uncertainty. Use sample agreement as the measure and add hedges from it, not the reverse.

source: Wang et al. (2026) Are LLM Decisions Faithful to Verbal Confidence? (RiskEval)
finding: Models can state confidence but do not use it to decide whether to answer when errors are costly. Verbal confidence stays flat as the penalty rises and models almost never abstain.
numbers: Penalty swept 0 to 100 per wrong answer; models include Gemini-3-Flash, Llama4-Maverick, GPT-5-mini, GPT-5-nano; HLE, GPQA Diamond, GSM8K. Normalised utility collapses under high penalty because models keep answering even when abstaining is optimal.
limits: Exact per-model numbers not extracted from the text; a few frontier models only.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on the model to abstain on its own; put the threshold in the scaffold, applied to a measured signal.

source: Amit, Galil and El-Yaniv (2026) Evaluating LLM Uncertainty in Long-Form Generation Using Deterministic Ground Truth (SALT)
finding: With noise-free labels on long outputs, confidence ranking is poor at the single-claim (atomic) level but clearer at line level. Reasoning raises accuracy while lowering confidence ranking quality.
numbers: 50+ LLMs, six procedurally generated tasks. Logit-based confidence functions beat verbalized ones on ranking and calibration (paired Wilcoxon, p<0.05). Mediation: reasoning models look better calibrated but this is explained by higher precision (p<0.001), with no residual reasoning effect (p=0.567). Binned calibration minimises ECE but ranking degrades with answer length and corrupted prefixes.
limits: Synthetic deterministic tasks, not open-ended agent work; logit-based so partly out of reach for APIs.
agent_relevance: Score long agent outputs per step or per line, not per atom; one confidence for a whole trajectory hides where the error is.

source: Zhao et al. (2026) SeSE: Black-Box Uncertainty Quantification Based on Structural Information Theory
finding: A claim-level extension of semantic entropy works on long-form text by splitting into atomic claims and building a claim-to-sample graph; verbalized uncertainty is a weak baseline.
numbers: Five LLMs, 24 model-dataset combinations. Llama-3.1-8B: +15.3% AUROC and +14.4% AURAC over semantic entropy; DeepSeek-V3.1: +5.21% AUROC and +1.57% AURAC over the second-best discrete SE.
limits: Long-form factual generation (claim matching by entailment), not multi-step agent action sequences; authors' own benchmarks.
agent_relevance: Cluster-agreement signals extend to long text if claims are extractable; for agent trajectories the matching step is the unsolved part.

source: Fleming, Ryu, Golfinopoulos and Rees (2014) Domain-specific impairment in metacognitive accuracy following anterior prefrontal lesions
finding: Causal follow-up to the 2010 grey-matter result: anterior PFC lesions impair perceptual but not memory metacognition, so the region is not domain-general.
numbers: Anterior PFC lesion n=7, temporal lesion n=11, healthy n=19. Perceptual meta-d'/d': group effect F(2,34)=5.78, P=0.007; anterior PFC below controls t(24)=3.67, P=0.001. Memory group effect F(2,34)=0.75, P=0.48. Group x domain interaction P=0.010. Perceptual meta-d'/d' 95% CI 0.28-0.64 vs memory 0.78-1.29.
limits: Very small patient group; lesions heterogeneous; first-order performance matched, so the deficit is metacognitive.
agent_relevance: Confidence is a separable monitor with domain-specific parts; supports separate per-domain monitors and cross-checks in the agent, not one global confidence.

source: Molenberghs et al. (2016) Neural correlates of metacognitive ability and of feeling confident: a large-scale fMRI study
finding: Larger-N fMRI (N=308) in a social/cognitive reasoning task: better metacognitive accuracy goes with LOWER anterior medial prefrontal activation; trial-level confidence maps to striatum and hippocampus. Higher confidence went with lower metacognitive accuracy.
numbers: N=308. Effect is a decrease in activation in anterior medial PFC, not the grey-matter volume correlate of Fleming 2010. Abstract read via Europe PMC; full text unavailable (server error).
limits: Abstract only; different measure (activation not volume), different task. Not a direct structural replication.
agent_relevance: Partial support for anterior PFC involvement at larger N; no direct large-N replication of the BA10 volume effect was found.

source: Hiremath and Hiremath (2026) Calibration Drift Under Reasoning
finding: A proposed account (hypothesis lock-in) says more reasoning budget can increase overconfidence. Empirical support is thin.
numbers: Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-3.3-70B, 47 reasoning-trap questions, four budgets, three seeds, 1,368 API calls, only 574 valid responses. 8B shows non-monotonic ECE; 70B inconclusive.
limits: Tiny, small models, many invalid responses; hypothesis only. Mei 2025 gives the better-supported version.
agent_relevance: Do not cite as evidence; note as a hypothesis for budget-vs-calibration.
